arxiv-1701-06233.title: What the Language You Tweet Says About Your Occupation
arxiv-1701-06233.creator: Tianran Hu, Haoyuan Xiao, Jiebo Luo, Thuy-vy Thi Nguyen
arxiv-1701-06233.description: Abstract Many aspects of people’s lives are proven to be deeply connected to their jobs. In this paper, we first investigate the distinct characteristics of major occupation categories based on tweets. From multiple social media platforms, we gather several types of user information. From users’ LinkedIn webpages, we learn their proficiencies.

arxiv-2106-00411.title: WebMIaS on Docker Thanks: The second author’s work was graciously funded by the South Moravian Centre for International Mobility as a part of the Brno Ph.D. Talent project. Affiliation: Faculty of Informatics, Masaryk University, Brno, Czech Republic
arxiv-2106-00411.creator: Dávid Lupták, Vít Novotný, Michal Štefánik, Petr Sojka
arxiv-2106-00411.description: Abstract Math informational retrieval (MIR) search engines are absent in the wide-spread production use, even though documents in the STEM fields contain many mathematical formulae, which are sometimes more important than text for understanding. We have developed and open-sourced the WebMIaS MIR search engine that has been successfully deployed in the European Digital Mathematics Library (EuDML).

arxiv-2209-09254.title: Pair density wave order from electron repulsion
arxiv-2209-09254.creator: Yi-Ming Wu, P. A. Nosov, Aavishkar A. Patel, S. Raghu
arxiv-2209-09254.description: Abstract A pair density wave (PDW) is a superconductor whose order parameter is a periodic function of space, without an accompanying spatially-uniform component. Since PDWs are not the outcome of a weak-coupling instability of a Fermi liquid, a generic pairing mechanism for PDW order has remained elusive. We describe and solve models having robust PDW phases.

arxiv-2212-02996.title: BC-VAD: A Robust Bone Conduction Voice Activity Detection
arxiv-2212-02996.creator: Niccolò Polvani*, Damien Ronssin, Milos Cernak
arxiv-2212-02996.description: Abstract Voice Activity Detection (VAD) is a fundamental module in many audio applications. Recent state-of-the-art VAD systems are often based on neural networks, but they require a computational budget that usually exceeds the capabilities of a small battery-operated device when preserving the performance of larger models.

arxiv-2302-00633.title: Deep Dependency Networks for Multi-Label Classification
arxiv-2302-00633.creator: Shivvrat Arya, Yu Xiang, Vibhav Gogate
arxiv-2302-00633.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Shivvrat Arya, Yu Xiang, Vibhav Gogate. We propose a simple approach which combines the strengths of probabilistic graphical models and deep learning architectures for solving the multi-label classification task, focusing specifically on image and video data. First, we show that the performance of previous approaches that combine Markov Random Fields with neural networks can be modestly improved by leveraging more powerful methods such as iterative join graph propagation, integer linear programming, and ℓ 1 \ell_{1} regularization-based structure learning.

arxiv-2501-11946.title: Towards Solutions of Manipulation Tasks via Optimal Control of Projected Dynamical Systems
arxiv-2501-11946.creator: Anton Pozharskiy, Armin Nurkanović, Moritz Diehl
arxiv-2501-11946.description: Abstract We introduce a modeling framework for manipulation planning based on the formulation of the dynamics as a projected dynamical system. This method uses implicit signed distance functions and their gradients to formulate an equivalent gradient complementarity system. The optimal control problem is then solved via a direct method, discretized using finite-elements with switch detection [ 16 ] .

arxiv-2505-03022.title: An Introduction to Topological Data Analysis Ball Mapper in Python
arxiv-2505-03022.creator: Simon Rudkin
arxiv-2505-03022.description: Abstract Visualization of data is an important step in the understanding of data and the evaluation of statistical models. Topological Data Analysis Ball Mapper (TDABM) after Dłotko, 2019 , provides a model free means to visualize multivariate datasets without information loss.

pmc-10707221.title: A Novel Lipase from Streptomyces exfoliatus DSMZ 41693 for Biotechnological Applications
pmc-10707221.creator: Guillermo Rodríguez-Alonso, Juan Toledo-Marcos, Lara Serrano-Aguirre, Carlos Rumayor, Beatriz Pasero, Aida Flores, Ana Saborido, Pilar Hoyos, María J Hernáiz, Isabel de la Mata, Miguel Arroyo, Salvatore Fusco, Patrizia Contursi
pmc-10707221.description: Genome mining of Streptomyces exfoliatus DSMZ 41693 has allowed us to identify four different lipase-encoding sequences, and one of them (SeLipC) has been successfully cloned and extracellularly expressed using Rhodococcus sp. T104 as a host. SeLipC was purified by one-step hydrophobic interaction chromatography. The enzyme is a monomeric protein of 27.6 kDa, which belongs to subfamily I.

pmc-11329664.title: Quantifying biomolecular organisation in membranes with brightness-transit statistics
pmc-11329664.creator: Falk Schneider, Pablo F. Cespedes, Narain Karedla, Michael L. Dustin, Marco Fritzsche
pmc-11329664.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Cells crucially rely on the interactions of biomolecules at their plasma membrane to maintain homeostasis. Yet, a methodology to systematically quantify biomolecular organisation, measuring diffusion dynamics and oligomerisation, represents an unmet need. Here, we introduce the brightness-transit statistics (BTS) method based on fluorescence fluctuation spectroscopy and combine information from brightness and transit times to elucidate biomolecular diffusion and oligomerisation in both cell-free in vitro and in vitro systems incorporating living cells.

pmc-11390260.title: Improving intravesical botulinum toxin-A injection technique: Reshaping the needle may benefit more
pmc-11390260.creator: Farooq Hameed, Adeel Anwaar, Riyan Imtiaz Karamat, Mamoona Anwar
pmc-11390260.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Graphical Abstract To the editor: Botulinum toxin, a purified neurotoxin extracted from clostridium botulinum, primarily works by blocking signal transmission at the neuromuscular junction through the inhibition of acetylcholine release. Recent studies suggest that botulinum toxin may also impact the release of other sensory neurotransmitters like substance P and ATP, while decreasing the axonal presence of capsaicin and purinergic receptors [1].

pmc-11508858.title: Essential Genes Discovery in Microorganisms by Transposon-Directed Sequencing (Tn-Seq): Experimental Approaches, Major Goals, and Future Perspectives
pmc-11508858.creator: Gemma Fernández-García, Paula Valdés-Chiara, Patricia Villazán-Gamonal, Sergio Alonso-Fernández, Angel Manteca
pmc-11508858.description: Essential genes are crucial for microbial viability, playing key roles in both the primary and secondary metabolism. Since mutations in these genes can threaten organism viability, identifying them is challenging. Conditionally essential genes are required only under specific conditions and are important for functions such as virulence, immunity, stress survival, and antibiotic resistance.

pmc-11715722.title: Care negotiation between people living alone with dementia in the United States and non‐kin caregivers
pmc-11715722.creator: Jane Lowers, Colby Smith, Kaitlyn Brus, Molly Perkins, Kenneth Hepburn

pmc-12474211.title: Epidemiological and Clinical Characteristics of Stenotrophomonas maltophilia Isolates from Hospitalized Medical Patients; An Emerging Pathogen in the Non-Critically Ill
pmc-12474211.creator: Dimitrios Kouroupis, Charalampos Zarras, Maria Zarfeiadou, Christos Sanos, Elias Iosifidis, Chrysi Michailidou, Konstantina Mpani, Panagiotis Pateinakis, Theocharis Koufakis, Michail Doumas, Ioannis Goulis, Dimitrios Vlachakis, Athina Pyrpasopoulou, Eric James Nilles
pmc-12474211.description: Until recently, Stenotrophomonas maltophilia was considered a low-virulence pathogen, usually found as an environmental commensal and colonizer of moist abiotic surfaces. Lately, it has increasingly been implicated in invasive infections with high associated morbidity and mortality. Most epidemiological studies involving patients with S. maltophilia infections have recorded risk factors and their associations with outcomes in critically ill patients.

pmc-12512292.title: Preparing graduate students for collaborative practice in chronic care: a mixed-methods evaluation of an interprofessional student-led education module
pmc-12512292.creator: Yaël Slaghmuylder, Gabriël Cantaert, Peter Pype, Pauline Boeckxstaens
pmc-12512292.description: BackgroundInterprofessional collaboration has become indispensable in chronic care. Embedding interprofessional education (IPE) in health-related curriculums can prepare students to be fit for practice in this interprofessional field. However, further research is required on the design of IPE to underpin and monitor modules.

pmc-12603581.title: Impact of Connected Mental Health on the Work Environment of Mental Health Clinicians: Protocol for a Systematic Literature Review
pmc-12603581.creator: Shweta Premanandan, Sofia Ouhbi, Magdalena Ramstedt Stadin, Charlotte Blease, Åsa Cajander, Maria Hägglund
pmc-12603581.description: BackgroundMany mental health professionals face work-related stress due to high job demands, limited control, and inadequate institutional support. Connected mental health (CMH) technologies such as mobile apps and teletherapy platforms are increasingly being proposed as tools to alleviate these job demands.

pmc-12976272.title: Metabolic reprogramming in cancer: dysregulation of glucose, lipid, and amino acid pathways and therapeutic opportunities
pmc-12976272.creator: Mingkang Yu, Di Yang, Xiuli Chen, Yuling Yang, Bingqiang Zhang, Xinxin Jiang, Lijie Xing, Yuxuan Yang, Yani Sun, Ning Li
pmc-12976272.description: Metabolic reprogramming is a hallmark of cancer, including hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Cancer cells exhibit enhanced glucose and glutamine uptake, increased glycolysis, pentose phosphate pathway activity, de novo lipogenesis, and altered amino acid metabolism. However, the metabolic crosstalk underlying cancer progression and the strategic directions for drug development remain insufficiently synthesized.

pmc-13203225.title: Integrated Omics Analysis of the Effects of Nano-Antimicrobial Peptide on the Intestinal Microbiota and Metabolome of Tibetan Sheep
pmc-13203225.creator: Yaqin Zhao, Xiaoshan Wang, Haixia Jing, Liyuan Zhao, Fengjun Liu
pmc-13203225.description: Simple SummaryNano-antimicrobial peptides are considered promising alternatives to conventional antibiotics. This study found that dietary supplementation with nano-antimicrobial peptides significantly affected the small intestinal microbiota of Tibetan sheep and altered the levels of conjugated bile acids, intermediate metabolites involved in phospholipid metabolism, and unsaturated fatty acids.
